1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing chess game with more challenging bots and character commentary, then add move sounds, threat and legal-move indicators, a game-over screen, and a review screen with accuracy, move grades, and an advantage tracker.

## Requirements
- User’s original feedback: they are around 1700 Elo on chess.com and easily beat this game’s bot labelled 2500.
- Add a sound on every move and a distinct check sound.
- Show threats and indicate legal destinations when a piece is selected.
- Show a game-over screen and an analysis screen with accuracy percentages, good/bad move grades, and an advantage indicator from start to finish.

## Decisions
- Use browser speech synthesis for optional spoken bot commentary.
- Extend the local chess search rather than integrating an external engine; ratings remain estimates, not official Elo.
- Run deeper bot search in a web worker to avoid blocking the UI.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added two higher-rated bot profiles and increased the engine’s supported strength levels.
- Added bot dialogue and an optional voice toggle in `index.html`, `app.js`, and `style.css`.
- Added iterative deepening and quiescence search, plus a worker for bot turns.
- Added `evaluatePosition` and `analyzeGame` exports to `src/chess.js`.
- Syntax checks and `git diff --check` completed without output; changes are uncommitted.

### Active
- Implement requested move/check sounds, threat indicators, legal-move cursor/indicators, game-over screen, analysis UI, and live advantage tracking.
- Connect the new `analyzeGame` helper to saved move history and render review results.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add move and check sounds, preferably with lightweight browser-generated audio.
2. Add visual threat markers and improve selected-piece legal destination cues.
3. Build game-over and analysis overlays, including white/black accuracy, per-move grades, and a move-by-move evaluation graph/advantage marker.
4. Save move records in history in the format expected by `analyzeGame`, wire analysis controls, and test the complete game flow.
5. Address engine performance: initial-position measurements were 12.9s at level 5, 18.7s at level 6, and 50.9s at level 7; consider tightening limits or optimizing before relying on the highest level.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: game layout, bot voice control insertion, opponent list.
- `app.js`: bot/game flow, dialogue, move history, UI event handlers.
- `src/chess.js`: chess rules, search engine, and newly added evaluation/analysis exports.
- `src/bot-worker.js`: background bot search.
- `style.css`: game styling and dialogue additions.

## Important Context
- Existing analysis helper currently accepts `plies` entries containing `{ position, move }`; current `app.js` history entries do not yet record moves, so this must be wired up.
- Voice commentary is currently configured with `en-US`; the interface and original request are Turkish, so consider localizing speech if appropriate.
- Engine timing test finished successfully and returned legal moves; the deepest level is very slow in the starting position.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the chess game with stronger bots and character commentary, then add move/check sounds, threat and legal-move indicators, a game-over screen, and move-by-move analysis.

## Requirements
- User is around 1700 Elo on chess.com and easily beats the bot labelled 2500.
- Add a sound for each move and a distinct check sound.
- Show threats and legal destinations when a piece is selected.
- Show a game-over screen and an analysis screen with player accuracy, move grades, and an advantage tracker from start to finish.

## Decisions
- Use browser speech synthesis for optional spoken bot commentary.
- Extend the local chess search rather than integrate an external engine; bot ratings are estimates, not official Elo.
- Run bot search in a web worker to avoid blocking the UI; game review also uses a worker.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added stronger bot profiles and increased supported search levels; added dialogue and optional voice toggle.
- Added iterative deepening, quiescence search, and `src/bot-worker.js`.
- Added `evaluatePosition` and `analyzeGame` in `src/chess.js`.
- Added generated move/check sounds, threat markers, and legal-destination cues.
- Added game-over and review overlays with accuracy, move grades, and a white-perspective advantage graph.
- Saved pre-move positions and moves in history for analysis; added `src/review-worker.js`.
- Syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed; a one-move analysis smoke test returned results.

### Active
- Validate complete browser game flow and review behavior; inspect potential accuracy/grade and advantage-evaluation issues.
- Assess engine responsiveness at higher strengths before relying on the top levels.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the app and test moves, check sounds, threatened-square and legal-move cues, undo/restart, game-over, and review.
2. Check review output on longer and varied games; improve analysis estimates if needed.
3. Reassess the highest bot strength, which may take a long time to search.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: game flow, sounds, indicators, overlays, history, and review rendering.
- `index.html`: game UI and overlay markup.
- `style.css`: game, threat, and review styling.
- `src/chess.js`: chess rules, bot search, position evaluation, and analysis.
- `src/bot-worker.js`: background bot search.
- `src/review-worker.js`: background game analysis.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Engine timing from the initial position: level 5 took 12.9s, level 6 took 18.7s, and level 7 took 50.9s.
- Review labels and accuracy are based on a shallow local estimate, not an external engine or official rating.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the chess game with stronger bots and character commentary, plus move/check sounds, threats and legal-move indicators, a game-over screen, and move-by-move analysis.

## Requirements
- The user is around 1700 Elo on chess.com and easily beats the bot labelled 2500.
- Add a sound for each move and a distinct check sound.
- Show threats and legal destinations when a piece is selected.
- Show a game-over screen and an analysis screen with player accuracy, move grades, and an advantage tracker from start to finish.

## Decisions
- Use browser speech synthesis for optional spoken bot commentary.
- Extend the local chess search rather than integrate an external engine; bot ratings are estimates, not official Elo.
- Run bot search and game review in web workers to avoid blocking the UI.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added stronger bot profiles, iterative deepening, quiescence search, bot and review workers, and optional voiced character commentary.
- Added move/check sounds, threatened-square and legal-destination indicators, game-over and review overlays, accuracy estimates, move grades, and a white-perspective advantage graph.
- Saved pre-move positions and moves in history for analysis.
- Passed JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.
- Tested in headless Chromium: initial board renders 64 squares, selecting e2 shows legal destinations e3/e4, and e2–e4 triggers a bot response.

### Active
- Validate complete browser flow, including check sounds and indicators, undo/restart, game-over and review overlays.
- Evaluate review results on longer games and refine shallow local accuracy/grade estimates if needed.
- Reassess responsiveness at the highest bot strengths.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Exercise the full game flow in a browser, including check and game-over conditions, review, undo, and restart.
2. Test review output on longer games and inspect rating/grade and advantage evaluation quality.
3. Reassess top-level engine response time.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game flow, sounds, indicators, overlays, history, review rendering, and bot worker integration.
- `index.html`: Board and overlay markup.
- `style.css`: Board indicators and game/review overlay styling.
- `src/chess.js`: Rules, bot search, position evaluation, and analysis.
- `src/bot-worker.js`: Background bot search.
- `src/review-worker.js`: Background game analysis.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Prior bot timings: level 5 took 12.9s, level 6 took 18.7s, and level 7 took 50.9s.
- Review labels and accuracy are based on a shallow local estimate, not an external engine or official rating.
- A one-move analysis smoke test returned output; in the browser, e2–e4 led to a bot reply and the human turn resumed.

## Objective
- Improve the chess game with stronger bots, character commentary, move/check sounds, threats and legal-move indicators, game-over and move-by-move analysis screens.
- Add sound, opening theory and general chess principles to the review experience, and make the interface clean and mobile-friendly.

## Requirements
- Bots should be challenging for a player around 1700 chess.com Elo; stronger bots should avoid nonsensical openings.
- Use opening theory for bots, and show central control and general chess principles in review.
- Mark book moves with a book icon, best moves with a star, and bad moves with a red exclamation mark.
- Show a sound for every move and a distinct sound for check.
- Show threats and legal destinations when selecting a piece.
- Include a game-over screen, player accuracy, move grades, and a start-to-finish advantage tracker.
- Keep the interface simple, attractive, and mobile-friendly.

## Decisions
- Use browser speech synthesis for optional spoken bot commentary.
- Extend the local chess search rather than integrate an external engine; ratings and review estimates are not official Elo.
- Run bot search and game review in web workers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added stronger bot profiles, iterative deepening, quiescence search, bot and review workers, and optional voiced character commentary.
- Added move/check sounds, threatened-square and legal-destination indicators, game-over and review overlays, accuracy estimates, move grades, and a white-perspective advantage graph.
- Saved pre-move positions and moves in history for analysis.
- Passed JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.
- Browser-tested legal indicators, a move and bot reply, undo, restart, and a 16-ply review with accuracy figures and an advantage chart.

### Active
- Add opening-book guidance to higher-strength bot move selection.
- Expand review with opening-book indicators, move-quality icons, central-control and general chess-principle feedback.
- Improve mobile layout and validate responsive behavior.
- Finish browser verification of terminal game flow, sounds, and threat indicators; a terminal test is running in the background.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the result of the running browser test when it completes; it was set up to exercise move/check sounds, threatened squares, checkmate overlay, and review entry.
2. Implement and test opening guidance for bots, prioritizing sound development and central control without overriding tactical search.
3. Add opening/book, best-move, and mistake indicators plus central-control/general-principle feedback to the review.
4. Refine mobile styles and test the game and review at narrow viewport widths.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game flow, sounds, indicators, overlays, history, and review rendering.
- `src/chess.js`: Rules, bot search, position evaluation, and analysis.
- `src/bot-worker.js`: Background bot search.
- `src/review-worker.js`: Background game analysis.
- `index.html`: Board and overlay markup.
- `style.css`: Main and responsive interface styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; modified files include `app.js`, `index.html`, `src/chess.js`, and `style.css`; new files include `src/bot-worker.js` and `src/review-worker.js`.
- Prior bot timings: level 5 took 12.9s, level 6 took 18.7s, and level 7 took 50.9s.
- Review grades and accuracy use shallow local estimates rather than an external engine or official rating.
- Earlier browser testing confirmed legal destinations e3/e4 from e2, undo/restart behavior, and a 16-half-move review. A later terminal-game test was not yet confirmed.

## Objective
- Improve the chess game with stronger bots, character commentary, move/check sounds, threats and legal-move indicators, game-over and move-by-move analysis screens.
- Add opening theory and general chess principles to review, and keep the interface clean and mobile-friendly.

## Requirements
- Bots should challenge a player around 1700 chess.com Elo; stronger bots should avoid nonsensical openings.
- Use opening theory for bots, and show central control and general chess principles in review.
- Mark book moves with a book icon, best moves with a star, and bad moves with a red exclamation mark.
- Show a sound for every move and a distinct sound for check.
- Show threats and legal destinations when selecting a piece.
- Include a game-over screen, player accuracy, move grades, and a start-to-finish advantage tracker.
- Keep the interface simple, attractive, and mobile-friendly.

## Decisions
- Use browser speech synthesis for optional spoken bot commentary.
- Extend the local chess search rather than integrate an external engine; ratings and review estimates are not official Elo.
- Run bot search and game review in web workers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added stronger bot profiles, iterative deepening, quiescence search, bot and review workers, and optional voiced character commentary.
- Added move/check sounds, threatened-square and legal-destination indicators, game-over and review overlays, accuracy estimates, move grades, and a white-perspective advantage graph.
- Saved pre-move positions and moves in history for analysis.
- Passed JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.
- Browser-tested legal indicators, a move and bot reply, undo, restart, and a 16-ply review with accuracy figures and an advantage chart.

### Active
- Opening-book data and helper functions were added in `src/chess.js`, but are not yet integrated into bot move selection or review.
- Add review icons, book-move annotations, central-control and general-principle feedback.
- Refine mobile styles and validate responsiveness.
- Confirm terminal-game browser test results; the test was backgrounded and remains unfinished.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Integrate opening guidance into bot selection without overriding tactical search.
2. Extend game analysis with book status, move-quality icon metadata, central-control data, and general-principle feedback; render these in the review.
3. Refine mobile layout and test narrow viewport widths.
4. Check the pending browser test result when available, then verify terminal flow, sounds, and threat indicators.

## Relevant Files
- `src/chess.js`: Search, opening-book lines/helpers, and game analysis.
- `app.js`: Game flow, sounds, indicators, overlays, history, and review rendering.
- `index.html`: Board and overlay markup.
- `style.css`: Main and responsive interface styling.
- `src/bot-worker.js`: Background bot search.
- `src/review-worker.js`: Background game analysis.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; modified files include `app.js`, `index.html`, `src/chess.js`, and `style.css`; new files include `src/bot-worker.js` and `src/review-worker.js`.
- Added opening lines in `src/chess.js`: Ruy Lopez, Italian Game, Queen’s Gambit Declined, Sicilian, French, Caro-Kann, London, King’s Indian, and Scotch.
- Added `bookOptions`, `centralControl`, and `principleFor` helpers in `src/chess.js`; they are not yet used.
- Prior bot timings: level 5 took 12.9s, level 6 took 18.7s, and level 7 took 50.9s.
- Review grades and accuracy use shallow local estimates rather than an external engine or official rating.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the chess game with stronger bots, character commentary, move/check sounds, threats and legal-move indicators, game-over flow, and move-by-move review.
- Include opening theory and general chess principles in review while keeping the interface clean and mobile-friendly.

## Requirements
- Bots should challenge a player around 1700 chess.com Elo; stronger bots should avoid nonsensical openings.
- Use opening theory for bots, and show central control and general chess principles in review.
- Mark book moves with a book icon, best moves with a star, and bad moves with a red exclamation mark.
- Show a sound for every move and a distinct sound for check.
- Show threats and legal destinations when selecting a piece.
- Include a game-over screen, player accuracy, move grades, and a start-to-finish advantage tracker.
- Keep the interface simple, attractive, and mobile-friendly.

## Decisions
- Use browser speech synthesis for optional spoken bot commentary.
- Extend the local chess search rather than integrate an external engine; ratings and review estimates are not official Elo.
- Run bot search and game review in web workers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added stronger bot profiles, iterative deepening, quiescence search, bot and review workers, and optional voiced character commentary.
- Added move/check sounds, threatened-square and legal-destination indicators, game-over and review overlays, accuracy estimates, move grades, and a white-perspective advantage graph.
- Saved pre-move positions and moves in history for analysis.
- Added opening-book guidance to bot search and review, with searched-score checks to avoid overriding clearly stronger tactical moves.
- Added book-move and best/weak-move icons, opening identification, central-control data, and general-principle move notes to review.
- Previously passed JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`; browser-tested move indicators, bot reply, undo, restart, and a 16-ply review.

### Active
- Refine mobile styles and validate responsiveness.
- Confirm terminal-game browser test results; verify terminal flow, sounds, and threat indicators after the latest changes.
- Re-run syntax checks and `git diff --check` after the latest edits.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run syntax checks and `git diff --check`; inspect the latest opening-book and review changes for correctness.
2. Test review rendering, opening recognition, icons, and principle notes in a browser.
3. Test narrow viewport widths and refine the mobile review layout if needed.
4. Verify terminal game flow, sounds, and threat indicators; resolve any pending browser test result.

## Relevant Files
- `src/chess.js`: Search, opening-book lines/helpers, and game analysis.
- `app.js`: Game flow, bot history handoff, sounds, indicators, overlays, and review rendering.
- `index.html`: Board and overlay markup, including opening insight.
- `style.css`: Main and responsive interface styling.
- `src/bot-worker.js`: Background bot search and opening-history input.
- `src/review-worker.js`: Background game analysis.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; modified files include `app.js`, `index.html`, `src/chess.js`, and `style.css`; new files include `src/bot-worker.js` and `src/review-worker.js`.
- Opening lines cover Ruy Lopez, Italian Game, Queen’s Gambit Declined, Sicilian, French, Caro-Kann, London, King’s Indian, and Scotch.
- Bot timings previously observed: level 5 took 12.9s, level 6 took 18.7s, and level 7 took 50.9s.
- Review grades and accuracy use shallow local estimates rather than an external engine or official rating.

## Objective
- Improve the chess game with stronger bots, character commentary, move/check sounds, threats and legal-move indicators, game-over flow, and move-by-move review.
- Include opening theory and general chess principles in review while keeping the interface clean and mobile-friendly.

## Requirements
- Bots should challenge a player around 1700 chess.com Elo; stronger bots should avoid nonsensical openings.
- Use opening theory for bots, and show central control and general chess principles in review.
- Mark book moves with a book icon, best moves with a star, and bad moves with a red exclamation mark.
- Show a sound for every move and a distinct sound for check.
- Show threats and legal destinations when selecting a piece.
- Include a game-over screen, player accuracy, move grades, and a start-to-finish advantage tracker.
- Keep the interface simple, attractive, and mobile-friendly.

## Decisions
- Use browser speech synthesis for optional spoken bot commentary.
- Extend the local chess search rather than integrate an external engine; ratings and review estimates are not official Elo.
- Run bot search and game review in web workers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added stronger bot profiles, iterative deepening, quiescence search, bot and review workers, and optional voiced character commentary.
- Added move/check sounds, threatened-square and legal-destination indicators, game-over and review overlays, accuracy estimates, move grades, and a white-perspective advantage graph.
- Saved pre-move positions and moves in history for analysis.
- Added opening-book guidance to bot search and review, with searched-score checks to avoid overriding clearly stronger tactical moves.
- Added opening identification, book/best/weak-move icons, central-control data, and general-principle move notes in review.
- Passed JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` after the latest edits.

### Active
- Validate review rendering, opening recognition, icons, and principle notes in a browser.
- Test narrow viewport responsiveness and refine mobile review layout if needed.
- Verify terminal-game flow, sounds, and threat indicators.

### Blocked
- Browser automation is not set up in the repo; Chromium is installed, but Playwright/Puppeteer/Selenium were not found.

## Next Move
1. Run browser-based checks for move indicators, bot reply, undo/restart, review, and terminal flow; use Chromium directly or set up an available test method.
2. Check review display and mobile layout at narrow widths; adjust styles if needed.
3. Re-run syntax checks and `git diff --check` after any changes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/chess.js`: Search, opening-book helpers, move evaluation, and game analysis.
- `app.js`: Game flow, bot/review worker handoff, sounds, indicators, overlays, and review rendering.
- `index.html`: Board and overlay markup, including opening insight.
- `style.css`: Main and responsive interface styling.
- `src/bot-worker.js`: Background bot search and opening-history input.
- `src/review-worker.js`: Background game analysis.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; modified files are `app.js`, `index.html`, `src/chess.js`, and `style.css`; new files are `src/bot-worker.js` and `src/review-worker.js`.
- Opening lines cover Ruy Lopez, Italian Game, Queen’s Gambit Declined, Sicilian, French, Caro-Kann, London, King’s Indian, and Scotch.
- Bot timings previously observed: level 5 took 12.9s, level 6 took 18.7s, and level 7 took 50.9s; ratings and review results are local estimates.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the browser chess game with stronger bots, helpful commentary and indicators, and a polished move-by-move review.
- Keep the interface clean and mobile-friendly.

## Requirements
- Challenge players around 1700 chess.com Elo; stronger bots should avoid nonsensical openings.
- Use opening theory and general chess principles in review; mark book, best, and weak moves with icons.
- Include move and check sounds, threats and legal destinations, game-over flow, accuracy, move grades, and an advantage tracker.
- Keep rating and review estimates clearly identified as unofficial.

## Decisions
- Use browser speech synthesis for optional spoken bot commentary.
- Extend the local chess search rather than integrate an external engine; ratings and review estimates are not official Elo.
- Run bot search and game review in web workers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added stronger bot profiles, iterative deepening, quiescence search, opening-book guidance, and bot/review workers.
- Added optional voiced commentary, move/check sounds, threats and legal-move indicators, game-over and review overlays, accuracy estimates, move grades, and an advantage graph.
- Added opening identification, book/best/weak-move icons, central-control data, and general-principle move notes.
- Browser smoke-tested initial board, legal indicators, a bot reply, undo, review rendering/opening recognition/chart, restart, and 360px mobile layout; no horizontal overflow.
- JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Verify terminal-game flow and move/check sounds in a browser; further inspect threat indicators during play.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test checkmate/draw game-over flow and move/check sounds in a browser.
2. Re-run syntax checks and `git diff --check` after any changes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/chess.js`: Chess rules, search, opening-book helpers, move evaluation, and game analysis.
- `app.js`: Game flow, workers, sounds, indicators, overlays, and review rendering.
- `index.html`: Board and overlay markup.
- `style.css`: Main and responsive interface styling.
- `src/bot-worker.js`: Background bot search.
- `src/review-worker.js`: Background game analysis.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: modified `app.js`, `index.html`, `src/chess.js`, and `style.css`; added `src/bot-worker.js` and `src/review-worker.js`.
- Opening lines cover Ruy Lopez, Italian Game, Queen’s Gambit Declined, Sicilian, French, Caro-Kann, London, King’s Indian, and Scotch.
- Bot timings previously observed: level 5 took 12.9s, level 6 took 18.7s, and level 7 took 50.9s.

## Objective
- Improve the browser chess game with stronger bots, helpful commentary and indicators, and a polished move-by-move review.
- Keep the interface clean and mobile-friendly.

## Requirements
- Challenge players around 1700 chess.com Elo; stronger bots should avoid nonsensical openings.
- Use opening theory and general chess principles in review; mark book, best, and weak moves with icons.
- Include move and check sounds, threats and legal destinations, game-over flow, accuracy, move grades, and an advantage tracker.
- Clearly identify ratings and review estimates as unofficial.

## Decisions
- Use browser speech synthesis for optional spoken bot commentary.
- Extend the local chess search rather than integrate an external engine; ratings and review estimates are not official Elo.
- Run bot search and game review in web workers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added stronger bot profiles, iterative deepening, quiescence search, opening-book guidance, and bot/review workers.
- Added optional voiced commentary, move/check sounds, threats and legal-move indicators, game-over and review overlays, accuracy estimates, move grades, and an advantage graph.
- Added opening identification, book/best/weak-move icons, central-control data, and general-principle move notes.
- Browser-tested board, legal indicators, bot reply, undo, review/chart/opening recognition, restart, and 360px mobile layout without horizontal overflow.
- Verified Scholar’s Mate checkmate flow, game-over overlay, king check indicator, and check tones; corrected the checkmate summary wording.
- Verified checkmate, stalemate, insufficient-material, and fifty-move-rule status handling.
- JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game flow, workers, sounds, indicators, overlays, and review rendering.
- `src/chess.js`: Chess rules, search, opening-book helpers, move evaluation, and game analysis.
- `index.html`: Board and overlay markup.
- `style.css`: Main and responsive interface styling.
- `src/bot-worker.js`: Background bot search.
- `src/review-worker.js`: Background game analysis.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: modified `app.js`, `index.html`, `src/chess.js`, and `style.css`; added `src/bot-worker.js` and `src/review-worker.js`.
- Opening lines cover Ruy Lopez, Italian Game, Queen’s Gambit Declined, Sicilian, French, Caro-Kann, London, King’s Indian, and Scotch.
- Previously observed bot timings: level 5 took 12.9s, level 6 took 18.7s, and level 7 took 50.9s.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the browser chess game with stronger, responsive bots, helpful commentary and indicators, and polished move-by-move review.
- Fix the reported sound issue (“Ses açılmıyor”) by clarifying and enabling move sounds separately from spoken commentary.

## Requirements
- Bots should be challenging without thinking more than 5–6 seconds per move.
- Keep the interface clean and mobile-friendly.
- Identify ratings and review estimates as unofficial.

## Decisions
- Use browser speech synthesis for optional spoken bot commentary.
- Use synthesized tones for move and check sounds.
- Keep ratings and review estimates local and unofficial.
- Add a dedicated move-sound toggle distinct from the existing speech toggle; keep move sounds off by default until the user enables them, to comply with browser audio gesture restrictions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added stronger bots, iterative deepening, quiescence search, opening-book guidance, bot/review workers, and a 5-second search deadline.
- Added commentary, move/check tones, legal-destination and threat indicators, game-over flow, review overlays, unofficial accuracy estimates, move grades, and advantage graph.
- Added separate “Sound on/off” and “Voice on/off” controls; audio context resume is awaited before playing tones.
- Syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed after the sound changes.

### Active
- Verify move sounds in a real browser after enabling them, including player and bot replies; test the controls on mobile layout.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Browser-test the sound toggle and synthesized move/check audio after a user gesture; confirm bot replies also sound.
2. Fix any remaining audio or layout problems, then rerun syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Audio synthesis, sound and speech toggles, move handling and sound calls.
- `index.html`: Separate sound and voice toggle markup.
- `style.css`: Dialogue row and toggle layout, including mobile styles.
- `src/chess.js`: Search engine and 5-second time limit.
- `src/bot-worker.js`: Bot search worker.
- `src/review-worker.js`: Review analysis worker.

## Important Context
- The only initial audio control was `#voice-toggle`, which controls speech synthesis rather than move sounds.
- Move sounds are now controlled by `#sound-toggle` and disabled by default; enabling it plays a test tone. Audio errors remain silently caught.
- Changes are uncommitted; the working tree already contains broader game improvements in addition to the audio fix.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the browser chess game with stronger, responsive bots, helpful commentary and indicators, and polished move-by-move review.
- Fix move sounds and keep them separate from spoken commentary.

## Requirements
- Bots should be challenging without thinking more than 5–6 seconds per move.
- Keep the interface clean and mobile-friendly.
- Identify ratings and review estimates as unofficial.

## Decisions
- Use browser speech synthesis for optional spoken bot commentary and synthesized tones for move/check sounds.
- Keep separate “Sound on/off” and “Voice on/off” controls; move sounds default off to respect browser audio gesture restrictions.
- Keep ratings and review estimates local and unofficial.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added stronger bots, iterative deepening, quiescence search, opening-book guidance, bot/review workers, and a 5-second search deadline.
- Added commentary, legal-destination and threat indicators, game-over flow, review overlays, unofficial accuracy estimates, move grades, and advantage graph.
- Implemented separate sound and voice toggles; verified sound enabling, player and bot move tones, sound-off behavior, and mobile layouts at 320px and 390px.
- Syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, audio synthesis and controls, bot turns, commentary, and review.
- `index.html`: Game interface and separate sound/voice controls.
- `style.css`: Layout and responsive styling.
- `src/chess.js`: Search engine and review analysis.
- `src/bot-worker.js`: Bot search worker.
- `src/review-worker.js`: Review analysis worker.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; working tree includes broader chess improvements in addition to the audio fix.
- Browser verification found no page errors; default sound toggle state is off and matches its label.

- Normal hamle, taş alma ve şah için farklı sesler eklendi.
- Tehdit ünlemi oyun sırasında kaldırıldı.
- Oyun bitince eski hamleleri inceleyebileceğiniz analiz ekranı eklendi; hamle notları, doğruluk çubukları ve avantaj grafiği gösteriliyor. Doğruluk ve değerlendirmeler yerel, resmî olmayan tahminlerdir.
- Sade bir açılış ekranı eklendi.
- Ses ve sesli yorum kontrolleri birbirinden ayrıldı.
